source_snapshot.test_name: Check BMC share and dedicate LAN at the same time
source_snapshot.items: Check BMC share and dedicate LAN at the same time
source_snapshot.procedure: Test three physical cable states: both dedicated and shared ports connected, shared connected/dedicated disconnected, and dedicated connected/shared disconnected.
source_snapshot.criteria: Both paths are reachable in the both-connected state; only the physically connected shared path is reachable in shared-only; only the physically connected dedicated path is reachable in dedicated-only.
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: DeepSeek correctly identifies physical recabling as human work but incorrectly treats that boundary as making the whole test non-automatable; it notes that an agent can report channel binding but does not define path-specific evidence.

original_test_intent.purpose: Verify BMC management reachability through the shared and dedicated LAN ports across the exact three required physical cable states, without a surviving path or cached session masking failure of the port under test.
original_test_intent.target: The specified BMC shared management port, dedicated management port, their BMC LAN channel/interface/MAC/IP bindings, and the designated test-client and switch paths.
original_test_intent.scope: Establish the approved isolated two-port topology, capture identity and mapping, have an operator set both-connected, shared-only and dedicated-only cabling in order, and automatically prove the expected reachable and unreachable path in each state using path-pinned fresh connections and link/counter evidence.
original_test_intent.operation: Label and map both physical paths; record baseline configuration without changing it; for each scenario have the operator establish and photograph/record the cable state, wait the owner-defined link/address convergence interval, close stale sessions/caches as specified, run fresh path-specific BMC reachability and identity checks, capture switch/link/channel evidence, then restore the approved final topology.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: One complete observation of each of the three distinct cable scenarios. The 10-minute attended and machine estimates do not define convergence timeout or justify omitting any scenario.
original_test_intent.expected_result: Both physical paths independently reach the same intended BMC in the both-connected state; shared-only reaches through the shared path and cannot reach through the disconnected dedicated path; dedicated-only behaves conversely; no loop, duplicate address, wrong target, unexpected failover path or persistent management loss occurs.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: Signed port/channel/interface/MAC/IP/VLAN/switch-client path map; BMC/firmware identity; per-scenario operator cable-state record; link state and switch-port counters; fresh path-pinned reachability and authenticated BMC identity; read-only LAN/channel data; timestamps, convergence/timeout, unexpected logs and restored final state.
ambiguities: The source does not define the port/channel/MAC/IP/VLAN topology or how a client proves which physical path carried a successful connection.
`Client can connect` has no protocol, fresh-session rule, timeout, retry or identity check.
The criteria can be satisfied superficially by the surviving port unless traffic is pinned and correlated to switch/link counters.
No final desired cable topology or behavior for shared/dedicated addresses that are equal, different or failover-capable is stated.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly preserves all three cabling states, physical operator control, isolated topology, per-scenario evidence and recovery. Its MANUAL ONLY verdict conflicts with V3's hybrid boundary because physical recabling is only the stimulus/setup; path-specific reachability and channel evidence are meaningful machine-verifiable acceptance activities.

applicable_history.decision: The old NO verdict treats physical recabling as the entire execution mode and does not recognize automated verification after each operator transition.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Reclassify MANUAL ONLY to REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION. An operator must move and verify the two cables, but the three-state reachability, BMC identity and path-correlation evidence can and should be automated after the topology and recovery contract are approved.

available_now: The test's three physical cable states and expected active/inactive paths are understandable.
Read-only BMC LAN/channel configuration and client reachability can be collected without changing network settings.
OpenBMC's ipmitool guidance documents `lan print [channel]` as a read operation distinct from `lan set`.
missing_inputs: Physical shared/dedicated port labels and BMC channel/interface/MAC/IP bindings, switch ports, VLANs and client source interfaces/routes
Path-pinning method, authenticated BMC identity check, link/address convergence wait, attempt count and success/failure timeout for each port
Expected simultaneous-port behavior, equal/different IP or failover rules, final cable state and approved handling of ARP/neighbor/session caches
Isolated topology, loop/duplicate-IP protection, alternate recovery path, operator transition evidence and network/BMC owner approval
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The BMC/network owner supplies bindings and expected dual-port behavior; the lab/network owner supplies isolated switch/client paths, loop controls and recovery; the onsite operator establishes and attests each cable state.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Record BMC identity, firmware, current LAN/channel data, interfaces, addresses and non-secret routing/topology evidence.
Validate the client-side path-pinning and identity-check method against the baseline without moving cables or changing BMC/switch configuration.
prohibited_until_closed: Do not recable production/unknown networks, modify BMC LAN/VLAN/routing, reuse a stale session as reachability proof, or create a loop/duplicate-address condition.
Do not let an agent claim the physical state, infer the traversed port from a ping alone, remove the only recovery path or continue after wrong-target response/network instability.
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: Both cable paths are physically labeled and mapped end to end; path-pinned fresh checks identify the correct BMC and correlate with the intended link/counters; the isolated topology prevents loops/duplicate IP; alternate recovery and final restore are rehearsed and approved.

revision_candidate.test_name: BMC Shared and Dedicated LAN Three-State Connectivity
revision_candidate.purpose: Verify independent BMC connectivity through the shared and dedicated management ports in both-connected, shared-only and dedicated-only cable states.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: The exact platform/BMC recipe in an isolated two-path management network with signed physical-port, BMC-channel, MAC/IP, VLAN, switch-port and client-interface mappings plus alternate recovery.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Both labeled physical BMC LAN paths and the same authenticated target BMC across all three source-defined cable states; neither a generic management ping nor one surviving path substitutes for per-port proof.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: End-to-end two-port map; expected dual-port/failover/IP behavior; client path-pinning method; identity protocol; convergence, timeout and retry values; isolated topology; cache/session handling; operator transition record; final topology; approvals and recovery access.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Capture the read-only configuration baseline. For each state in order—both connected, shared only, dedicated only—the operator establishes and attests the cables; after the specified convergence interval the agent opens fresh path-pinned connections, authenticates the target BMC, tests both expected-positive and expected-negative paths, and correlates results with link/switch counters and read-only channel data. Restore and verify the approved final topology.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Correct BMC and physical labels verified; client routes/interfaces and switch ports mapped; both paths proven recoverable; topology isolated from loops/duplicate addressing; expected simultaneous-port behavior and timeouts specified; protected credentials, local/OOB recovery, operator and approvals available; no unrelated management changes in progress.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: BMC/firmware and signed path map; redacted LAN/channel baseline; operator cable-state and timestamps; per-state client source/path, fresh connection transcript, authenticated BMC identity, link state and switch counters for both paths; timeout results for expected-negative paths; logs, anomalies and restored final reachability.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The exact platform BMC networking specification and approved lab VLAN/routing topology; ipmitool documentation supports read-only channel collection but does not define this platform's shared/dedicated behavior.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Never move cables without the onsite operator, alter LAN/VLAN/routing during this test, connect both ports where a loop is possible, expose credentials, use cached sessions, remove the last recovery path or infer physical-path success from unpinned traffic.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: BMC and network owners approve mapping, simultaneous-port behavior and isolated topology. An onsite operator confirms and changes each physical cable state and can restore management access immediately.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Cable insertion/removal and physical-state attestation are manual. Fresh reachability, BMC identity, channel/link/counter correlation, timeout enforcement, log capture and result packaging are automated after each transition.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: On loop, duplicate address, wrong BMC identity, unexpected route, switch instability or management loss, stop testing, restore the approved cable topology through onsite/local access, clear only approved client caches/sessions, verify both intended interfaces and preserve all diagnostic evidence before retry approval.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Unresolved port/path map, no isolated topology/recovery/operator, ambiguous traffic path, wrong target, loop/storm/duplicate address, unexplained reachability through a disconnected path, failure of an expected active path, BMC/network instability or inability to restore the final topology.

identified_defects: V2 classifies the complete workflow MANUAL ONLY although automated path-specific connectivity evidence is central to acceptance.
The source lacks a method to distinguish the physical path used by successful traffic.
The source omits convergence, timeout, session/cache and final-topology rules.
reason_for_change: Apply the V3 hybrid-test rule: preserve operator-only recabling while recognizing automated per-state verification as a meaningful part of the requested test, and close the false-positive path where one surviving interface masks the other.

new_technical_evidence.title: OpenBMC IPMITOOL cheatsheet
new_technical_evidence.version: upstream master accessed 2026-10-13; platform build must be recorded
new_technical_evidence.applicability: OpenBMC/IPMI platforms exposing standard LAN channels; vendor mappings remain platform-specific
new_technical_evidence.supports: `ipmitool lan print [channel]` is a read-only configuration query and is technically distinct from `lan set`, supporting automated evidence collection after manual recabling.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The command cannot by itself prove which external physical port carried client traffic.

removed_ambiguities: Requires fresh path-pinned traffic and target identity instead of generic cached reachability.
Makes all three physical states separate mandatory observations.
Separates manual cable stimulus from automated acceptance evidence and names the final restore requirement.
resolved_blockers: Physical recabling does not prevent automated evidence collection; the hybrid workflow is technically executable once an operator and topology contract are supplied.
remaining_blockers: Execution still requires the platform-specific path map, expected simultaneous-port behavior, isolated network, onsite operator, explicit approval and alternate recovery.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 fixes the capability boundary without pretending an agent can move cables, adds end-to-end physical-path proof that prevents failover/caching false positives, and retains V2's loop, duplicate-IP, management-loss and restore safeguards.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The isolated validator correctly separated manual cable changes from automated fresh path-pinned BMC identity/connectivity checks across all three required states.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: The source mandates both-connected, shared-only and dedicated-only cable states and opposite per-port connectivity results in the two single-port states.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 correctly safeguards physical recabling but labels the full test MANUAL ONLY despite machine-verifiable reachability/channel evidence after each human transition.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Require an operator for cables and an isolated mapped topology; automate only fresh path-pinned identity/reachability and link/counter evidence, with alternate recovery and final restore.
